answer.location_description: Top-right corner of the image, roughly the top 3-4 rows and the right half (columns ~14-22). A bright patch there pushes the output toward benign.
answer.shortcut_type: bright corner patch / artifact marker in top-right corner
answer.mechanism: Malignancy-promoting hidden units 10 and 16 (net positive paths through layer-2 units u4, u8, u13, u15 and away from u7, u9, u12) and the broad units 19 and 23 carry a block of strongly negative weights in the top-right corner. Brightness there suppresses these units and removes their malignant contribution. Benign-promoting centre-surround units (0, 8, 25, 5) have mildly positive weights in the same corner. Together these push a bright top-right corner toward a negative (benign) logit. Rough path sums: unit 10 about +20k and unit 16 about +36k in integer units toward the logit.
answer.evidence: Unit 19, rows 0-2, columns 12-23: weights of -35 to -72 (e.g. -72, -69, -70, -64, -61, -59). This contrasts sharply with its positive surround weights elsewhere, so it is not a smooth anatomical pattern. Unit 23, rows 0-2, columns 15-23: -38 to -60. Unit 10, rows 0-2, columns 14-21: -32 to -52. Unit 16, rows 0-3, columns 15-21: -30 to -56. These units are otherwise nodule-shape detectors (negative centre, positive ring), and the corner block is unrelated to the nodule at the centre. Benign units 0 and 8 show positive weights in the same corner (unit 0 r0-r3 c19-21: 33, 43, 41, 44; unit 8 r2-r4 c19-20: 40, 41, 49, 40). The block appears only in this corner, not symmetrically at other edges, so it does not look like chest wall anatomy.
answer.main_feature: Centre-surround filters on the central nodule (rows ~7-16, cols ~8-16) compare the bright core with its surroundings. Small compact bright cores with dark surround (units 0, 2, 5, 8, 13, 15 etc.) push toward benign. Larger nodules that fill the surrounding ring, possibly irregular (units 6, 9, 10, 12, 16, 30), push toward malignant.
